title: London Customs Accounts, 1380-1560: machine-readable data and research tools
description:
Machine-readable data and browser-based research tools for the particular customs accounts of the port of London, 1380-1560, produced by the project Unlocking Upcycled Medieval Data: North Sea Networks, People, and Commodities in the London Customs Accounts 1380-1560 (Institute of Historical Research, University of London, and Otto-Friedrich-Universität Bamberg).

The London particular customs accounts are the largest surviving serial collection of medieval trade documents in Europe. This dataset "upcycles" existing scholarly transcripts of those accounts — semi-structured text prepared over decades for human readers — into structured, linkable data: 33,548 ladings across 46 account-book files; a curated glossary of 3,333 commodity headwords aligned to Getty AAT and Wikidata; and 246,008 person mentions grouped for identity matching across 37,693 surname and 5,632 forename forms.

Contributions. Justin Colson and Werner Scheltjens conceived the project and secured its funding, and direct it as co-investigators. Stephen Gadd designed and built the data pipeline, the reconciliation and annotation tools, and the published site. Eliot Benbow and María Grove-Gordillo carried out the historical and linguistic curation: commodity glossary curation, and expert annotation of the cargo entries, including the independent double annotation from which the project's inter-annotator agreement is measured.

Rights. Licensing differs by component. Site code (JavaScript, HTML, CSS) is MIT; project-authored data is CC BY 4.0; material deriving from earlier editions and reference works is released only as its rights position is cleared. See docs/data-licensing.md in the repository for the per-file position, which governs where it differs from the single licence recorded here.
notes:
This version contains no data files. It carries the project's descriptive and citation metadata and its licence position, and nothing else. It is published to establish a persistent identifier and an agreed authorship record while rights clearance for the underlying transcripts is completed.

The data described above will appear in later versions under this same concept DOI, which always resolves to the most recent one. Cite this version where the reference is to the project and its team; cite a later version where the reference is to data.
